title: Can You Hop to the Last Square?

concept.title: Walk from left to right and remember the farthest square you can still reach
body: You stand on the first of `n` squares in a row. From the square `i` you may hop **any distance from 1 up to `a[i]`** to the right (a square with `a[i] = 0` is a dead end). Can you reach the last square? For `2 3 1 1 4` yes: hop 1 square, then 3 squares to the end. For `3 2 1 0 4` no: every route gets stuck on the square with the 0.

Let `reachable(i)` be true if some route ends on square `i`. The square `i` is reachable if some earlier reachable square `j` can hop far enough: `j + a[j] >= i`. Checking all earlier squares is O(n^2). But we only need **the farthest square that is reachable by any hop so far**: call it `far`. All squares up to `far` are reachable (squares in between can be hopped over to by shorter hops), so the square `i` is reachable exactly when `i <= far`, and then it extends the reach: `far = max(far, i + a[i])`.

body.code:
far = 0                                   # the farthest square reachable so far
ok = True
for i in range(n):
    if i > far:                           # square i cannot be reached: we are stuck
        ok = False
        break
    far = max(far, i + a[i])
print("yes" if ok else "no")

body: The key is that reachability is **monotone**: reachable squares fill a block from the start, with no gaps, because a hop of any shorter length is also allowed. The whole table of "reachable or not" shrinks to one number, and the time is O(n), the memory O(1). If the loop finishes without getting stuck, the last square is reachable.

statement: There are `n` squares in a row. From the square `i` (counting from 0) you may hop to the right by any distance from 1 to `a[i]` squares (not at all if `a[i] = 0`). You start on the square 0. Print `yes` if you can reach the square `n - 1`, otherwise print `no`.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of squares.
The second line has `n` numbers: `a[i]` is the longest hop you may make from the square `i`.

examples.note: Every route ends on the square 3, where the hop length is 0: no.

hints: Keep the farthest square that can be reached so far.
If the current square is farther than that, you are stuck.
Otherwise the farthest reach becomes max(far, i + a[i]).

explanation: The squares that can be reached form a block from the start, so only the farthest reachable square is kept: if the current square lies beyond it we are stuck, otherwise the reach grows to max(far, i + a[i]). Reaching the end of the loop means the last square is reachable.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

far = 0
ok = True
for i in range(n):
    if i > far:
        ok = False
        break
    far = max(far, i + a[i])
print("yes" if ok else "no")
